original_card.one_sentence_claim: SBT proves that a single globally consistent time coordinate across closure protocols exists if and only if the discrete time-translation 1-form omega on the protocol graph is exact (every loop has zero holonomy), and shows this is the SAME closed-but-not-exact H^1 / telescoping criterion that governs the cycle-affinity arrow-of-time audit (P6) and the force-implies-cycles no-go, thereby compressing 'no global time,' 'thermodynamic arrow,' and 'force needs cycles' into one cohomological loop-integral mechanism.
original_card.target_known_fact: The integrability/exactness criterion for a global time function: a discrete 1-form admits a global potential t with omega(u->v)=t(v)-t(u) iff every directed cycle sum vanishes; nonzero loop holonomy obstructs a global potential. Discrete analogue of the clock-synchronization gap / non-integrable simultaneity in rotating frames (Sagnac) and of spacetimes lacking a global time function; the thermodynamic arrow is the companion nonzero-cycle-affinity (Schnakenberg/Gaspard) instance.
original_card.minimum_viable_result: In the finite protocol-graph laboratory, a global time potential exists iff omega is exact; the noncommuting protocol triangle exhibits nonzero holonomy (H approx 0.5) while the commuting control gives H=0, so no single global time coordinate exists in the noncommuting regime. Telescoping triviality once the 1-form model is granted.
original_card.baseline_comparison: RECOVERY / REORGANIZATION, not improvement. Core is textbook discrete Hodge / integrability criterion plus Schnakenberg/Gaspard cycle affinity; the relativistic/Sagnac connection is analogy only.
